newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian private bank to increase capital, expand.
newsitem.headline: Croatian private bank to increase capital, expand.

text.p: Croatia's private Kaptol Banka plans to increase its capital by five million German marks to 15 million to expand its business, bank officials said on Friday.
"We are obliged to increase the bank's capital by next February, to meet the Central bank's threshold required for full banking licence," spokeswoman Lidija Maricic told Reuters.
She could not say how Kaptol, which grew within a year from a small savings bank, was going to raise the necessary sum.
Among the bank's plans for next year were also the founding of a life-insurance company and an investment fund.
The bank is 40 percent owned by small private shareholders. The rest is split between various companies and the grandson of Croatian president Franjo Tudjman.
Kaptol deals with small and medium-range firms, but plans to introduce loans to citizens, probably in 1997, Maricic said. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
